learning_outcomes.text: Apply acquired basic knowledge to examples of mechanical and thermal process engineering.
Independently recognize relationships, initiated by understanding process engineering processes (e.g., separation, mixing, distillation).
Safely identify, describe, analyze, and evaluate occurring process engineering problems.
Derive scientifically sound judgments about the mode of operation and demonstrate them in further new applications and recognize interface problems.
Work together on tasks and problems in a team in interdisciplinary cooperation.

syllabus_topics: Reading and creating P&ID flow diagrams
Tasks and basic concepts of mechanical process engineering (material and energy balances of physical processes)
Fundamentals of particle technology: Description of particle systems (e.g., residual moisture, particle size distribution)
Fundamentals and applications of mechanical separation technology (Stokes settling velocity, clarification area)
Methods for solid-liquid separation: Sedimentation, filtration, centrifugation (plate separator and decanter centrifuge)
Description of separation processes - fields of application for industrial centrifuges (wastewater treatment plant; dairy; ..)
Constructive design and functionality of industrial centrifuges
Fundamentals and applications of mechanical mixing and separation technology: Sieving and sorting; crushing, mixing and stirring
Fundamentals and applications of thermal process engineering: Distillation; evaporation and condensation; drying; crystallization
Processes and applications of gas-gas separation (e.g., membrane separation processes, adsorption)
Processes and applications of gas-solid separation (e.g., filtration, cyclone separation, scrubbers)
Introduction to chemical process engineering (using the example of an integrated steelworks)
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination.
